test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 26 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: For a data, if the mean is 28.5 and the median is 32, then the mode using empirical formula is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Relationship** between measures of central tendency:

**Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**

Substitute the values: Mode = 3 × 32 − 2 × 28.5

Mode = 96 − 57 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** of the data = 28.5

**Median** of the data = 32

**Formula Used:**

For a moderately skewed distribution: **Mode = 3(Median) − 2(Mean)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edac693489da00dcc38ad76d189ba24efd8440fe6fa02b7c3163d099a5347335.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × 32 − 2 × 28.5

⇒ Mode = 96 − 57

⇒ Mode = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

Karl Pearson established this relation for **moderately skewed distributions**: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the values of Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Mean and Median Formulas

Mean = (∑x)/n | Median is the **(n+1)/2th** term for odd n, and the average of **n/2th** and **(n/2 + 1)th** terms for even n.

Skewness

If Mean > Median > Mode, the distribution is **positively skewed**; if Mode > Median > Mean, it is **negatively skewed**.</p
